newsitem.title: MEXICO: CNN sees doubling Spanish-language viewers in 1997.
newsitem.headline: CNN sees doubling Spanish-language viewers in 1997.

text.p: CNN expects to more than double viewership of its Spanish-language channel in Latin America to nine million from the current four million by the end of the year, company officials said on Thursday.

CNN launched its 24-hour Spanish-language news channel throughout Latin America on March 14 and at the same time became the first U.S.-based news organisation to open a news bureau in Cuba since 1969.

"We see a brilliant future (in Latin America). Currently we have more than four million subscribers. We hope by the end of the year to have a penetration in the total market ... of nine million subscribers," Rolando H. Santos, vice president for CNN en Espanol, told a news conference.
While CNN is expanding in Latin America, NBC pulled the plug on its Spanish-language network at the end of March.
But there is still plenty of competition among 24-hour news networks in Latin America with CBS Telenoticias, owned by Westinghouse, and ECO, which is part of Mexico's Televisa.
CNN is a part of Atlanta-based Turner Broadcasting System, which merged with Time Warner last year.
